sources.content: In §4 'F>0 at d0' is not automatic; it is the imposed C4-cell condition d0<x1 (already in the W_I chain). The forced location becomes x1∈(0,r). The W_I definition and all theorems are unchanged.

self_recheck_of_341LF_dependency: Reread v5 §§3-4 in raw. The three-finite-group exclusion was redone: contact gives (ατ0+βτ1)-(ατ2+βτ3)V_j=0 at three distinct V_j, hence T=(z-β/α)(τ3z²+τ1), which has imaginary roots; α=0 forces β=0. The quadratic case is likewise ruled out. Positive-contact component nonvanishing and the absence of an ω=1 contact were reread. No defect found. This is an owner self-check only.
structural_observations_this_interval_no: In word I, H=F2-S=P2/(Oplus*E_B) has poles that interlace exactly: x1<oU1<x2<oL2<x3<oU3. The double zeros r,s,w sit in the intervals (x1,oU1),(oU1,x2),(x3,oU3); P3's c and 1/c sit in (x2,oL2),(oL2,x3). Orientation at a C2 contact is fixed by which side of the oU1 pole it lies on.

With psi=P2/P3: psi-1=ΔE*E_B/P3, so psi>1 on (0,x1)∪(x2,x3) and psi<1 elsewhere, with psi(0)=psi(∞)=1. P4/P3=psi(1/t), and P1≥0 on the C1 cell is equivalent to psi(t)+psi(1/t)≥1. No contradiction was found.
No uniform emptiness proof and no point. A genuine resolution likely needs either a new extremal identity or a GO'd exact search of the explicit sets, which is not requested or admitted.
